newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares at 3-yr high but seen sputtering.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares at 3-yr high but seen sputtering.

text.p: The Austrian Traded Index (ATX) ended on a new three-year high on Thursday but traders said a lack of fresh capital entering the market indicated the rally was running out of steam.
The 21-share ATX ended 3.54 points, or 0.29 percent, firmer at 1,212.03 points, but closed below its intra-day high of 1,216.41 points.

"It's more likely that we will see 1,205 points than 1,220", one trader said, adding that liquidity was thinning out at higher levels. He saw the ATX in the next days in a range between 1,210 and 1,215 points.
Another trader also doubted that the market would rise further and forecast a consolidation.
"I dont see much room for the market to go up at moment", he said.
The trading session was characterised by interest in selective shares and also profit taking in some issues.
Among the ATX shares 12 stocks closed higher, seven were down and two remained unchanged.
Top gainer was Austrian microchip maker AMS, up 3.06 percent at 1,178 schillings.
VA Tech continued to rise and gained 11 schillings to close at 1,814. The technology group on Thursday reported a strong growth in sales and order intake in 1996.
Leading loser was rubber maker Semperit, whose shares were down 3.50 percent at 579 schillings.
Leykam-Muerztaler slipped back 0.68 percent to 305 schillings after it announced it would cancel its dividend for 1996 following a net loss at its KNP Leykam unit.
The ATX February future was up 2.0 points at 1,211.
